findings: SNL96 frame-with-brackets/caps consists of one bare frame, one bevel-gear case, two inside brackets, two outside brackets, two inside caps, two outside caps, twenty bracket-to-channel bolt assemblies and twenty MX13 bevel washers.

Bare frame has separate M373 top and M374 bottom channels, M375 middle diaphragm, M376/M377 inner angles, two M378 outer angles, two each M380/M382 inner gussets and M383/M384 outer gussets, four M338 brake suspension brackets and two M385 stops. SNL97 continues with eight rivet lengths, not eight individual rivets.

HB125 Plate78 / HB204 Plate121 and SNL Plate23 show vertically separated top/bottom channels behind the bevel case. The new bracket height of170mm is an unconstrained initial envelope; it is not proof of attachment to those channels. Reconstruct this vertical profile against the frame before accepting the casting.
HB134 requires casing installation before the epicyclic set, and documents chain-link cutaways in epicyclic gussets. It does not establish a new bearing-foot cutout through the casing sheet.

The outer foot profile in the horizontal Plate22 section intersects the current inferred casing sidewall. Preserve this conflict: the frame/body/casing relationship must be solved together. Do not rotate the fixed supports out of the aft-facing orientation or silently shorten the sourced foot width to clear it.
next_actions: Establish conditional frame-channel X/Z planes from SNL Plate2 and Plate23; retain scaling and placement uncertainty.
Build M373/M374 and M375-M384 frame skeleton around actual sleeves and rear bulkhead, documenting member sections and connection pads.
Determine the correct vertical bracket shape and chain/gusset passage; inspect joint sections and all interference regions.
Resolve or explicitly bound M391 foot count and interface before populating feet and holding hardware.
